edits.after: At $r=0$, $Q_0=p=p^{(0)}$ by [F2]. If $r<m$ and $p^{(r)}=Q_r$, termwise differentiation in [F3] kills the $k=r$ constant term and multiplies each term with $k>r$ by its exponent $k-r$; for each $k>r$, the resulting real coefficient is $a_k\bigl(\prod_{s=0}^{r-1}\iota(k-s)\bigr)\iota(k-r)=a_k\prod_{s=0}^{r}\iota(k-s)$. Indeed the finite natural product extends by its last factor, and [F7] carries that natural identity to the product of canonical real images. The new exponent is $(k-r)-1=k-(r+1)$, so the differentiated sum is exactly $Q_{r+1}$. Hence $p^{(r+1)}=Q_{r+1}$.

edits.before: Let $q$ be any formal polynomial of degree at most $n$ with $q(x_i)=y_i$. Extend the actual coefficient lists of $p$ and $q$ by zeros through index $n$, obtaining vectors $(a_k)$ and $(b_k)$; these are vectors for their evaluations, not padded formal objects. The vector $c_k=a_k-b_k$ defines by [F3] a formal polynomial $r$ of degree at most $n$; [F5] gives $r(t)=p(t)-q(t)$ for every real $t$. Since $p$ and $q$ agree at all nodes by step 1.1 and the choice of $q$, $r$ has the $n+1$ distinct roots $x_0,\ldots,x_n$. If $r$ were nonzero, [F4] would give at most $\deg r\le n$ roots, a contradiction. Hence $r$ is the zero formal polynomial; by [F3], every $a_k-b_k=0$. The canonical coefficient lists of $p$ and $q$ are therefore identical, so $p=q$.
edits.after: Let $Q$ be any formal polynomial of degree at most $n$ (allowing zero) with $Q(x_i)=y_i$, and denote its evaluation by $q(t):=Q(t)$. Extend the actual coefficient lists of $P$ and $Q$ by zeros through index $n$ (using all-zero vectors for zero polynomials), obtaining vectors $(a_k)$ and $(b_k)$; these describe their evaluations $p$ and $q$, not padded formal objects. The vector $c_k=a_k-b_k$ defines by [F3] a formal polynomial $r$ of degree at most $n$; [F5] gives $r(t)=p(t)-q(t)$ for every real $t$. Since $p$ and $q$ agree at all nodes by step 1.1 and the choice of $q$, $r$ has the $n+1$ distinct roots $x_0,\ldots,x_n$. If $r$ were nonzero, [F4] would give at most $\deg r\le n$ roots, a contradiction. Hence $r$ is the zero formal polynomial; by [F3], every $a_k-b_k=0$. The canonical coefficient lists of $P$ and $Q$ are therefore identical (or both objects are zero), so $P=Q$, and consequently $p=q$ as evaluation functions.
